questions.q: What does type() return for the value 129.99?
options: <class 'float'>
<class 'str'>
<class 'int'>
<class 'bool'>
questions.explain: 129.99 has a decimal point, which makes it a float, not an int.

questions.q: What does None represent in Python?
options: An explicit value meaning 'no value,' distinct from 0, an empty string, or False
An empty string
The same thing as the number 0
A syntax error
questions.explain: None is its own distinct value used to represent the absence of data.

questions.q: What happens when you try to run "2" * 129.99 in Python?
options: It silently returns 259.98
It returns the string '2' repeated 129 times
It automatically converts the string to an int first
A TypeError is raised, because a string can't be multiplied by a float
questions.explain: Python does not silently guess your intent across incompatible types — it raises a TypeError.

questions.q: What does the expression quantity > 0 and unit_price > 0 evaluate to if quantity is 3 and unit_price is 0?
options: It raises an error
None
False, because both conditions must be True for 'and' to return True
True, because at least one condition is True
questions.explain: The 'and' operator requires both sides to be True; here unit_price > 0 is False.

questions.q: Why would a quantity field read from a file commonly need int() applied before doing math with it?
options: Files never contain numeric data
int() is required before any variable can be printed
Values read from raw text commonly arrive as strings even when they look like numbers
int() makes the number display with more decimal places
questions.explain: Text read from a file is a string by default, so it must be explicitly converted before arithmetic.
